text: The last lesson laid out the brief and the symptom. This one builds the office network end-to-end and applies the troubleshooting methodology to find exactly where the connection to the cloud inventory system is breaking.

With roughly fifty devices to support, a /26 subnet comfortably covers the office — 64 total addresses, 62 usable — carved out of Northbridge Retail's larger private address space. Workstations and printers get addresses automatically from DHCP. The office's local servers get static addresses reserved outside the DHCP pool, so they never risk getting reassigned.

Chapter 5's methodology earns its keep here. Identify: the symptom is precise — only the cloud inventory system times out from this office, while every other office reaches it fine and every local resource works. That rules out the inventory system itself. Isolate: a ping to the inventory system fails, but a ping to the VPN gateway succeeds — the tunnel really is up, just like the teammate said. Test: checking the firewall's outbound rules at the office edge turns up the actual issue — a rule written for the checkout service was never updated to also cover the inventory system's IP range when it was added later. Resolve: adding that missing rule restores connectivity immediately.

This is the exact trap Chapter 5 warned about. "The VPN is up" was true, but it only guarantees the tunnel itself works — not that every device on the other end is allowed to send traffic through it. The firewall rule sitting in front of that tunnel was a separate, independent control, and it was the one actually blocking traffic, even though the tunnel underneath it was perfectly healthy.
With the network built and the fault found and fixed, the last step is turning this project into something that actually demonstrates what was learned — which is exactly what the final lesson covers.
